title: One review removed. Why didn’t the stars move?
seoTitle: Google Rating Unchanged After Removal? | ReputationResolved
description: An original 1,744-scenario model explains why a one-star review removal can leave the displayed Google rating unchanged. Download the data and method.
dek: An original model of 1,744 feasible rating states shows how a one-star removal can improve the average without changing the rounded score.
imageAlt: Modeled unchanged-score shares rise from zero at 10 and 25 starting reviews to 94.0 percent at 500 and 97.0 percent at 1,000 reviews.
datasetTitle: One-star removal and one-decimal score visibility
datasetDescription: 1,744 feasible mathematical starting states across seven review-count groups. Constructed model data, not business observations or removal success rates.
variables: Modeled one-decimal score before and after removal

title: No booking record? That doesn’t settle whether a review is fake.
seoTitle: No Customer Record for a Google Review? | ReputationResolved
description: Google review nicknames change what a customer-record search can prove. Explore 12 evidence scenarios, a source-linked matrix and a private evidence worksheet.
dek: A public display name is a search clue, not a customer ID. A source-linked guide to separating an unexplained review from a documented policy concern.
imageAlt: Twelve illustrative review-evidence cases mapped to three next steps: more context, policy assessment or Google's dedicated extortion report.
datasetTitle: Google review evidence: twelve illustrative cases
datasetDescription: An author-coded qualitative matrix of twelve constructed review-evidence examples with source links, inference limits and suggested reporting routes. Not Google decisions or measured customer outcomes.
